Teams assume Content Caching documentation covers storefront language. macOS caching server deployment and App Store Connect actually separate network cache workflows from product-page copy:

  • Content Caching on the Mac — when a Mac runs the Content Caching service under System Settings → General → Sharing, it stores local copies of Apple software updates, App Store downloads, iCloud content, and other Apple assets so devices on the same network can fetch from the peer cache. System caching behavior — outside AppLocale scope.

What macOS Content Caching actually does — listing honesty

Apple ships Content Caching as a macOS service under System Settings → General → Sharing on Mac computers. When enabled, the Mac acts as a caching server that stores local copies of Apple software updates, App Store app downloads, iCloud photos and documents, and other Apple content — allowing devices on the same network to download from the nearby peer cache instead of repeatedly fetching identical files from Apple's servers, reducing organization bandwidth usage. Third-party MDM, Mac-admin, and enterprise-mobility apps may complement this by monitoring cache status, reporting bandwidth savings, documenting caching server placement, or educating IT about Content Caching best practices. Content Caching–specific vocabulary — what translates differently in zh-Hans

Mac fleet bandwidth and caching server marketing on App Store pages uses vocabulary general localization guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese App Store readers evaluate Content Caching — not a literal paste of US marketing:

内容缓存 (Content Caching)

Apple's Chinese MDM and Mac-admin support materials use 内容缓存 for the macOS service that caches Apple software updates, App Store downloads, iCloud content, and other Apple assets locally on a Mac. Some fleet-admin marketing also uses Apple 内容缓存 when emphasizing the Apple-native caching path. AppLocale picks the term IT admins recognize on each screenshot — a status dashboard frame needs 内容缓存-friendly phrasing; a benefit headline may use Apple 内容缓存 when accurate to your English source.

缓存服务器 (caching server)

US pages use "Caching server" or "Mac caching server" when describing the Mac that runs Content Caching on the network. China storefront copy often uses 缓存服务器 when describing the local Mac that stores cached Apple content for fleet devices — distinct from generic CDN or web server terminology.

对等缓存 (peer cache)

Apple documentation describes devices downloading cached content from a nearby Mac on the same network as peer cache behavior. zh-Hans marketing uses 对等缓存 on frames that explain how managed devices fetch Apple updates and App Store downloads from a local cache instead of the internet — separate from iCloud sync or Personal Hotspot consumer tethering marketing.

带宽节省 (bandwidth savings)

The primary org benefit of Content Caching is reduced internet bandwidth when many devices download the same Apple software updates or App Store apps. zh-Hans copy uses 带宽节省 or 节省带宽 on benefit headlines and description paragraphs — the commerce hook Chinese IT buyers expect when evaluating caching server ROI.

Apple 软件更新缓存 / App Store 下载缓存

Content Caching stores multiple Apple content types — software updates, App Store app downloads, iCloud photos and documents, and more depending on cache configuration. zh-Hans copy may use 软件更新缓存 for OS update cache frames and App Store 下载缓存 for app download cache frames when your English source distinguishes cache types on separate gallery images.

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need Mac-admin search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 内容缓存, 缓存服务器, and 带宽节省 each signal different intent from 配置描述文件, VPP, or 托管 Apple ID keywords.
